versions.content:
# Auto claims guidelines (excerpts)

Authority: senior desk adjusters may pay up to $15,000 per claim (indemnity) and set reserves up to $25,000.
Above that, the supervisor; above $50,000 or any policy-limits demand, the Claims Manager.
Texas first-party deadlines (Ins. Code ch. 542): acknowledge, begin the investigation and request what you
need within 15 days of notice; accept or reject in writing within 15 business days of receiving all items
(business days exclude weekends and Texas holidays, including Veterans Day 11/11 and Thanksgiving 11/26-27); if
you need more time, tell the claimant why in writing, and decide within 45 days of that notice; pay within 5
business days of accepting.
Total losses: ACV from the CCC valuation, less the deductible; send the valuation report with the offer.
Owners may dispute with comparable vehicles; review them in good faith. The appraisal clause is available.
Liability: any time-limited demand, any demand at or above limits, or any claim with specials above 50% of the
limit is reported to the supervisor and Claims Manager the same day, with a copy to the insured (excess
letter) and defense counsel if in suit. Never let a time-limited demand lapse without a decision.
Fraud indicators: refer to SIU with the facts. Don't accuse, deny or delay a claim for suspicion alone;
continue handling in parallel unless SIU says otherwise.
Payments: confirm payee and amount against the file; report any duplicate or overpayment to Claims Payments.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
Part D, Coverage for damage to your auto: we pay for direct and accidental loss to your covered auto, minus the
deductible. Other than collision losses include hail.
Limit of liability: the lesser of the actual cash value of the stolen or damaged property, or the amount
necessary to repair or replace it.
Transportation expenses: up to $30 per day, to a maximum of $900, beginning 24 hours after a covered loss.
Appraisal: if we and you disagree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal.
Part A, Liability: bodily injury limits as shown on the declarations.
